results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Each of the 49 reverse-outline summaries matches the controlling idea of the spec paragraph it is aligned to, in the spec's order (intro p01-p04, scene p05-p09, needs p10-p16, pieces p19/p20/p17/p18, choices p21-p27, stages p31, practice p32-p41, wrong p42, conclusion p43-p50).

Each of the 49 reverse-outline summaries matches the controlling idea of the spec paragraph it is aligned to, in the spec's order (intro p01-p04, scene p05-p09, needs p10-p16, pieces p19/p20/p17/p18, choices p21-p27, stages p31, practice p32-p41, wrong p42, conclusion p43-p50).

results.quote: In practice the design comes down to four rules (carrier events, channel costs that change, one status endpoint, one refund command), the service rules of marketplaces, one worked order and a set of measures.
results.finding: The reverse outliner needed two summaries: a preview of the whole section and the first practice rule (carrier events, not polling). The spec's p32 controlling idea itself joins the section preview and the first rule in one paragraph, so the draft follows the spec; splitting needs a spec change (a separate lead-in unit or a shorter preview).

results.quote: The same parts give you a list for your own shop: for each promise it makes after checkout (delivery date, collection, refund, order status), name the system on the spot that knows the fact it depends on, the event that carries that fact and the measure that shows when the promise broke.
results.finding: The outliner needed two summaries: the common remedy pattern across Part IV (with five remedies recounted) and a forward checklist for the reader's own shop. The spec's p49 controlling idea assigns both the part's so-what and its take-away to this one paragraph; the draft follows it.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: scene and message map to S1/S2, status page and views to S3, state machines to S2, choices and stage rule to S3, self-service and refund command to S4, WISMO and the measures to S5, channel pricing and carrier events to S1, marketplace and AI-agent endpoint to S3; the part close performs the role the journal spec assigns.

results.draft_locus: How the Pieces Fit Together, the components table after Figure 4

results.draft_locus: Introduction ¶3, then What the Customer Needs ¶6 and the component table
results.quote: the documentation of platforms, helpdesks and carriers (Shopify, commercetools, Zendesk and others)
results.finding: 'Helpdesk' is on the does_not_know list. It is used in the introduction, in the WISMO paragraph and in the component table before any gloss; the first explanation by example ('a helpdesk such as Zendesk or Gorgias shows the platform's order next to the ticket') comes only in The Choices. No flow reader reported it, and the draft does gloss it eventually, so it is recorded uncorroborated.
The introduction opens with a puzzling scenario (three answers about one order), bridges to the systems that hold the facts and states the thesis; none of the weak patterns.

The conclusion answers the opening, sorts what is established from what depends on context and the author's synthesis, poses questions, closes the part as the journal spec assigns and hands off; it does not open with 'in conclusion', end on a rephrased thesis or add a new subtopic.

p43 joins the opening's three answers and the eleven tickets into one cause no section states alone; p48 sets the part's five cases as one problem; the so-what (three read models, WISMO beside the integration monitors, remedies as contracts and rules, a per-promise list for the reader's shop) is stated in p46 and p49.

'The customer of the opening had three answers because each view read a different system' returns to the introduction's customer; p48 returns to the Part IV opening's order confirmed in seconds, as callback.to declares.

The introduction reader predicted the three views and the systems feeding them, the separate states, WISMO as a measurement, the four options and scale, practice with marketplaces, Eva's messages 13-22 April and measures, the failure patterns, and the evidence (Kestrel & Pine's tickets, platform/helpdesk/carrier documentation, vendor contact data) and tone, matching the expected answer and the roadmap.

The reader named 'ships in two parcels' with the second's date, an OMS as the only possible emitter (none in the platform-only landscape), and that the page, notifications and agent read one record showing goods per line or parcel, money and return state rather than one word; matches the expected answer.

The reader named Schrödinger's Order (agent and page disagree because the helpdesk reads the platform) and the Message in a Bottle ('shipped' at label print), with the rules: the service view reads the owner of the goods state, re-point the helpdesk at the OMS, trigger 'shipped' on the carrier's handover scan with a working tracking link; matches the expected answer.

The reader said cancel only before the warehouse accepts the work (afterwards a request; refuse when unknown) and to count WISMO per shipped order (per 100, incl. peak), not as a share of tickets, as a signal of the integrations; matches the expected answer.
